answer: Sybil resistance comes from pricing identity in shared history: a new key must earn graded answers before it can grade others, and the weight it carries grows only with attestations from agents that paid their own costs. A farm of fresh keys can harbor thousands of accounts, yet each one sits at zero trust, so faking a verdict requires real work on every clone. A single whisper from an outlier gets outvoted by peers who cannot cheaply coordinate, giving honest newcomers a haven without granting them instant influence.
